title: Habitat Schoolhouse Preschool Workbook 5 — Part 2 (Letters S, T, U)
publisher: The Habitat Schoolhouse Inc / Gumboot Kid

activityTypes.description: Full-page watercolor illustration (pond animals on a log) with prompt: 'Look at the picture below and make up a silly story about what you see.' Oral storytelling from visual prompt.
activityTypes.skill: oral language, creative thinking, visual literacy

activityTypes.description: Letter Ss themed: 'Colour the BIG shapes blue and the SMALL shapes yellow.' Geometric shapes (circles, squares, hexagons, triangles) in a 2x2 grid. Combines letter-of-the-week (S for Small) with shape recognition and size comparison.
activityTypes.skill: math concepts (big/small, size comparison), shape recognition, following directions

activityTypes.description: Full-page watercolor animal (sloth, tiger) with labeled body parts (small black eyes, thick fur, long limbs, curved back, strong claws). Below: 'How many tails does the sloth have?' (dot-trace number) + 'Where do sloths sleep?' (multiple choice: Trees/Caves/Nests).
activityTypes.skill: science (animal anatomy), counting, reading comprehension, dot-tracing numbers
activityTypes.frequency: per letter section — animal name starts with the focus letter (S=Sloth, T=Tiger)

activityTypes.description: Letter Ss themed: 'Ss Strawberry — Place the right number of buttons, coins, stones or whatever item you choose onto each strawberry.' 4 numbered strawberries (1-4) in watercolor. Designed for lamination and reuse with physical counters.
'THE LETTER T — Colour and decorate the letters below.' Giant outline uppercase T and lowercase t filling the page. Child colors/decorates freely.
activityTypes.skill: letter recognition, fine motor, creative expression

activityTypes.description: 'Uu Uppercase — Colour or draw a circle around the uppercase letters.' Mixed uppercase and lowercase letters scattered across the page with watercolor cattails/dragonfly decorating the margins. 'How many uppercase letters did you find?' box at bottom.
activityTypes.skill: letter case discrimination, counting, visual scanning

letterOfTheWeek.description: Each section (S, T, U) has a consistent set of activities: counting mat, letter coloring, animal diagram, sorting activity, uppercase/lowercase identification. The letter appears in bold at the top of every page (Ss, Tt, Uu) with a themed word (Strawberry, Tiger, Uppercase).
letterOfTheWeek.value: Predictable structure. The child knows what kinds of activities to expect in each letter section.

watercolorNaturalistArt.description: Every illustration is watercolor naturalist — pond animals, botanical elements, realistic animal anatomy diagrams. The art is museum-quality, not clipart. Consistent with the Pond Map tracking system.
watercolorNaturalistArt.value: Beautiful enough that kids want to engage. The art makes the workbook feel special, not disposable.

multiModalPerLetter.description: Each letter section hits multiple skill areas: visual (letter identification), kinesthetic (coloring, placing manipulatives), oral (silly story), analytical (sorting, counting), and science (animal anatomy). Same multi-modal philosophy as Harcourt's alt teaching strategies, but embedded in the workbook itself.
multiModalPerLetter.value: Multiple ways to engage with each letter. Different skills reinforce the same content.

manipulativeIntegration.description: The counting mat pages are designed for physical manipulatives: 'Place the right number of buttons, coins, stones or whatever item you choose.' This echoes Carolyng's directive: suggest household items for manipulatives.
manipulativeIntegration.value: Concrete-to-abstract pathway. Physical objects before written numbers.

crossCurricularPerPage.description: The animal diagram pages combine science (anatomy), math (counting body parts), reading (multiple choice comprehension), and fine motor (dot-tracing numbers) in a single page. 4 subjects, one page.
crossCurricularPerPage.value: Maximum learning density without feeling crowded. The watercolor art does the heavy lifting.

overallLayout.structure: one activity per page, full-page illustrations
overallLayout.spacing: very airy — one concept per page, lots of art, minimal text
overallLayout.visualHierarchy: art-dominant — the watercolor illustrations are the centerpiece, text is secondary

difficulty.complexity: single-skill per page, multi-skill per section
difficulty.scaffolding: high — one concept per page, large illustrations, simple instructions

characters: themed animals per letter (sloth, tiger, etc.)
theming.colorPalette: full-color watercolors — greens, blues, warm naturals

printFormat.colorRequirement: needs color — the watercolor art is essential

gaps.name: animal-anatomy-diagram-page
gaps.description: Full-page watercolor animal illustration with labeled body parts + counting question (dot-trace number) + comprehension question (multiple choice). Combines science, math, reading, and fine motor in one page.

gaps.name: letter-section-bundle
gaps.description: A coordinated set of 5-6 activities all themed around one letter: counting mat, letter coloring, animal diagram, sorting activity, uppercase/lowercase identification, oral story prompt. Packaged as a mini-unit per letter.

notes: Fourth Aless drop. This is the STUDENT-FACING workbook that pairs with the Record Keeping system. Together they form a complete preschool curriculum: workbook (instruction) + pond map (progress tracking) + progress cards (assessment). The watercolor naturalist art style is EXACTLY what Carolyng identified as her preference — Aless independently chose the same aesthetic. This confirms both users share the Charlotte Mason / nature study art preference. The activity types map well to Homa's existing recipes (counting mat, coloring page) with two new gaps (animal anatomy diagram, letter section bundle).
